description: The top-block value is CONCAVE in the displacement vector -- every internal term is -eps(2d + (u_i - u_j)), concave composed with a linear map; every bulk tail is -eps(2d + u_i); the cost is -(ln q0/2) sum u^2 -- so maximising it over real u >= 1 is a concave program, a relaxation of the integer problem and hence a rigorous upper bound.  Its value B_relax = 2.2537 is 1.042x the integer maximum where #7349's B_sharp was 1.816x, and the resulting cut on the e_inf search falls from 90 to 27, which IS enumerable (~6e6 blocks) where 90 (~1e10) is not.  An intermediate Jensen bound is also recorded: valid, 2.6951 over the measured T range, cut 43, still not enumerable.  Gap G2 is REDUCED, NOT CLOSED: an unconditional closure still needs a certificate for the concave maximum (a tiny numerical gradient is not a proof) and a check of the block lengths between this probe's measured range and the rigorous T0.

constants._note: both suprema are over T <= T_measured_max, NOT over all T.  T0_rigorous is the length past which the per-row cap forbids reaching B_relax; T_measured_max+1 .. T0_rigorous is unchecked, which is why G2 is reduced rather than closed.

relaxation_P5.objective: Xblock(u) at real u, exactly -- no linearisation, no Jensen

jensen_P3.form: sum_i f(Delta_i) <= (T-d) f(mean),  f(x) = eps(2d) - eps(2d+x) concave

open_gaps.G2_remaining_a: a certificate for the concave maximisation -- the supergradient inequality at the returned point, with boundary coordinates carrying a non-positive gradient by KKT
open_gaps.G2_remaining_b: block lengths T = 13..40 are unmeasured; T0 = 40 is rigorous from the per-row cap turning negative at row 6
open_gaps.G1: unchanged: Xbot(s) <= Xblock(s) for every s, measured equal for s <= 12 and top-higher by 0.01982 at s = 13
open_gaps.headline: still the upper bound on M_n, which none of this touches

checks.name: P1 the real-u objective is the same function the integer enumeration maximised
checks.detail: F at the integer argmax reproduces #7349's enumerated maximum to -2.74e-26, and the Lambert tail resummation agrees with the direct sum to 3.155e-30 at 5 points.  Both matter: the relaxation is only a relaxation of the right problem if the extended function restricts correctly, and every evaluation here routes through the resummed tail rather than the sum #7349 used

checks.name: P2 the block value is concave in u — measured, not assumed
checks.detail: minimum concavity gap 0.00147382 over 200 random ordered triples.  The reason is one second derivative used three times: every internal term is `-eps(2d + (u_i - u_j))` up to a constant — concave composed with a linear map — every bulk tail is `-eps(2d + u_i)`, and the cost is `-(ln q0/2) sum u_i^2`.  This is what makes the relaxation to real u a CONCAVE PROGRAM rather than a search, so a coordinate-wise stationary point is the global maximum and not a local one

checks.name: P3 Jensen is a valid upper bound and saturates where the linear one runs away
checks.detail: 0 violations over 8 blocks.  The difference in kind shows at [8]: exact -1.1490916, Jensen -1.1490916 — equal, because a single-row block has no internal pairs and Jensen leaves the tail exact — against the linear bound's 2.8776793.  The linear bound claims a block worth MINUS one is worth nearly three, which is the whole of why B_sharp is 1.8x too big

checks.name: P4 B_sharp's slack is concentrated in row 0, and it is a missing cap
checks.detail: row 0's budget 2.893607227 is 73.79 % of B_sharp = 3.92139923, and it is attained at u_0 = 7.44745.  The true best single-row block is [3] at 0.9296691034 — 3.1125x less.  The per-row bound is the tangent at u = 0 and has no cap; the real gain saturates at S_e(1) = 2.568028 and then loses to the quadratic cost.  So the fix is not a better constant, it is a bound that bends

checks.name: P5 the relaxed sup is 1.04x the integer maximum, against B_sharp's 1.82x
checks.detail: B_relax = 2.2537313388386045641 at T = 7, argmax [3.9769, 2.794, 2.075, 1.5824, 1.231, 1.0, 1.0] — recognisably the integer argmax [4, 3, 2, 2, 1, 1, 1] with integrality let out.  That is 1.04349x the integer maximum 2.15980237612, where B_sharp was 1.81563x.  The AP ordering constraint was DROPPED from the program (a further relaxation, so the bound stays valid) and the optimum satisfies it anyway at every T: True

checks.name: P6 the relaxed bound turns the cut from unenumerable into enumerable
checks.detail: B_sharp cut at 90 (~1e10 blocks, hopeless); B_jensen at 43; B_relax at 27, which is 6,325,874 blocks — minutes, not geological time.  Inside any such cut the enumeration carries no effective cap, since entries >= 1 and sum <= L force length <= L and every entry <= L.  So the ARITHMETIC of an unconditional closure now works; what is missing is the certificate, not the compute

checks.name: P7 block length is rigorously bounded, and the unchecked window is explicit
checks.detail: every row past index 5 contributes at most `Ghat(i+1) - ln q0/2 < 0`, so the cumulative per-row cap falls below B_relax = 2.25373133884 at T0 = 40: no block of length > 40 can reach it.  This probe measured T <= 12, where the sup peaks at T = 7 and falls monotonically after.  So T = 13..40 is UNMEASURED — the gap between 'falls in the range I looked at' and 'falls forever' is exactly 28 values of T, and closing it is compute rather than insight

verdict: Concavity of the block value turns sup_s Xblock from a search into a concave program and shrinks gap G2 from 1.82x to 1.04x, taking the e_inf cut from an unenumerable 90 to an enumerable 27.  It does not close G2: the concave maximum is numerical and the block-length window between the measured range and the rigorous T0 is unchecked.  Both are finite specified computations rather than open questions, which is the change.
